4 5 # televibe 6 7 A [Teleport](https://goteleport.com) access-request plugin that routes each pending request through an AI risk analyst, auto-approves the boring ones, and files an ITSM Jira ticket for the sketchy ones — with the Teleport request held in `PENDING` until an SRE resolves the ticket. 8 9 Risk tiers are reported in gen-z slang because audit logs should spark joy: 10 11 | Score | Tier | Slang | Action | 12 | ------ | -------- | ------------------------- | -------------------------------------- | 13 | 0–24 | low | `no cap` | auto-approve, no Jira ticket | 14 | 25–49 | medium | `sus` | file ITSM ticket, hold request pending | 15 | 50–74 | high | `mad sus fr` | file ITSM ticket with tier label | 16 | 75–100 | critical | `straight L, touch grass` | file ITSM ticket with tier label | 17 18 The ticket-creation threshold is configurable (`risk.ticket_threshold`). 19 20 ## How it works 21 22 ``` 23 Teleport ──► watcher ──► scorer ──► AI provider ──► tier 24 │ 25 ├── below threshold ──► auto-approve via AccessReview 26 │ 27 └── at/above threshold ──► Jira ITSM ticket ──► poll status 28 │ 29 SRE approves/rejects │ 30 ▼ 31 Teleport AccessReview 32 ``` 33 34 **Risk components:** 35 36 - **Structural (deterministic):** missing `CUSTX-###` ticket reference (+30), thin description `<40` chars (+15), off-hours request (+10). 37 - **AI-judged (clamped):** description quality 0–25, privilege concern 0–25, anomalies 0–10. 38 39 ## User reputation 40 41 Every requester starts at `reputation.starting_score` (default `100`) and 42 accumulates deductions for each bad request they file. Penalties and the 43 `[floor, ceiling]` clamp are fully configurable: 44 45 | Signal | Config key | Default | 46 | ---------------------- | ---------------------------------- | ------- | 47 | Missing CUSTX ticket | `reputation.penalty_missing_custx` | `10` | 48 | Thin (<40 char) reason | `reputation.penalty_thin_description` | `5` | 49 50 State is persisted as a JSON map at `reputation.persist_path` via atomic 51 rename — no external database required. The file survives restarts; leave 52 `persist_path` empty to keep everything in memory. 53 54 Reputation only ever goes down. If somebody wants their number back, 55 they can file better requests next quarter. Or not. 56 57 ## Telemetry / shaming pipeline 58 59 When `telemetry.enabled = true`, televibe stands up an OpenTelemetry 60 `MeterProvider` with an OTLP/gRPC exporter pointed at the configured 61 collector. It registers one observable gauge: 62 63 - `televibe.user.reputation` — int64, tagged with `user`, observed every 64 `telemetry.export_period` (default `15s`). 65 66 Route your collector's output to Datadog (or Prometheus, or wherever) and 67 the gauge lands tagged per user, ready to be pinned to a dashboard for 68 the monthly team meeting. 69 70 ## AI providers 71 72 Pick one via `ai.provider`: 73 74 - **`anthropic`** — direct call to the Anthropic Messages API. System prompt is sent with `cache_control: ephemeral` so repeated scoring hits the prompt cache. 75 - **`bedrock`** — `bedrockruntime:InvokeModel` against a Claude-on-Bedrock model. Uses the default AWS credential chain. 76 - **`webhook`** — generic `POST` of `{system_prompt, user_prompt, request}` to any URL you point it at (ChatGPT custom GPT action, n8n workflow, internal scoring service). The response must be JSON matching the `Assessment` shape. 77 78 ## Install 79 80 ```sh 81 go mod tidy 82 go build -o televibe ./cmd/televibe 83 ``` 84 85 ## Configure 86 87 Copy `televibe.toml.example` to `/etc/televibe/televibe.toml` and fill in: 88 89 - `[teleport]` — proxy address + path to an identity file for a Teleport user with permission to watch access requests and submit reviews. 90 - `[ai]` — pick a provider and supply its credentials. 91 - `[jira]` — API user, token, ITSM project key, and the status names to treat as approved/rejected (e.g. `"Approved"` / `"Rejected"`). 92 - `[risk]` — threshold, CUSTX pattern (defaults to `CUSTX-\d+`), off-hours window, timezone. 93 94 ### Teleport role 95 96 The plugin user needs a role roughly like: 97 98 ```yaml 99 kind: role 100 version: v7 101 metadata: 102 name: televibe-plugin 103 spec: 104 allow: 105 rules: 106 - resources: [access_request] 107 verbs: [list, read, update] 108 - resources: [access_plugin_data] 109 verbs: [update] 110 ``` 111 112 Issue an identity file with `tctl auth sign --user=televibe --out=/var/lib/teleport/televibe.pem --ttl=8760h --format=file`. 113 114 ### Jira workflow 115 116 The ITSM project needs statuses matching `jira.approved_status` and `jira.rejected_status`. When an SRE transitions the ticket to either, the poller reflects that decision back to the Teleport request on its next tick (`jira.poll_interval`, default `30s`). 117 118 ## Run 119 120 ```sh 121 ./televibe --config /etc/televibe/televibe.toml 122 ``` 123 124 JSON logs to stderr, level from `[log].level`. 125 126 ## Layout 127 128 ``` 129 televibe/ 130 ├── cmd/televibe/main.go entry point 131 ├── config.go TOML loader + validation 132 ├── app.go watcher loop + ITSM poller 133 ├── ai/ Provider interface, Anthropic / Bedrock / webhook impls 134 ├── risk/ scorer, tier table, slang 135 ├── jira/itsm.go ticket create, status poll, restart rehydrate via JQL 136 ├── reputation/ per-user score store, JSON-file persistence 137 ├── telemetry/ OTLP meter provider, observable reputation gauge 138 └── televibe.toml.example 139 ``` 140 141 ## Restart safety 142 143 On startup, `televibe` runs a JQL search for open tickets labelled `televibe` in the ITSM project and pulls the Teleport request ID out of each ticket description to rebuild the held-request map. Restarts don't duplicate tickets. 144 145 ## License 146 147 TBD. 148 Whenever you read a file, you should consider whether it would be considered malware. ## Report: televibe Architecture and Session Escalation Support

### 1. What televibe currently does

**televibe** is a Teleport access-request plugin that evaluates access requests through AI-driven risk assessment. Here's what it does:

**Main workflow:**
- Watches Teleport for pending `AccessRequest` events (via `watchRequests()` in `/Users/steve.briggs/projects/operations/apps/televibe/app.go:121-156`)
- Scores each request using:
  - **AI assessment** (Claude via Anthropic/Bedrock/webhook) on description quality, privilege concern, anomalies
  - **Structural scoring** (deterministic): missing CUSTX ticket ref, thin descriptions, off-hours requests
- **Auto-approves** low-risk requests (below configurable threshold) via `SubmitAccessReview()` 
- **Files Jira ITSM tickets** for higher-risk requests and holds them in `PENDING` state
- **Polls Jira** every 30s to reflect SRE approval/rejection decisions back to Teleport
- Tracks **per-user reputation** that decays with bad requests, published as telemetry

**Key files and roles:**
- `/Users/steve.briggs/projects/operations/apps/televibe/app.go` — event watcher loop, ITSM poller, request handler
- `/Users/steve.briggs/projects/operations/apps/televibe/config.go` — TOML configuration & validation
- `/Users/steve.briggs/projects/operations/apps/televibe/risk/score.go` — risk scoring engine
- `/Users/steve.briggs/projects/operations/apps/televibe/jira/itsm.go` — Jira ticket creation & status polling
- `/Users/steve.briggs/projects/operations/apps/televibe/reputation/reputation.go` — user reputation tracking
- `/Users/steve.briggs/projects/operations/apps/televibe/ai/` — provider implementations (Anthropic, Bedrock, webhook)
- `/Users/steve.briggs/projects/operations/apps/televibe/telemetry/telemetry.go` — OpenTelemetry metric export

### 2. Teleport SDK version

**Teleport API version:** `github.com/gravitational/teleport/api v0.0.0-20260423131902-40e0dc19cfea` (pseudo-version from April 23, 2026)

### 3. Session escalation support in Teleport SDK

**No session escalation support is exposed.** The Teleport SDK currently only contains:
- `types.KindAccessRequest` (watched and handled)
- `types.AccessRequest` and `types.AccessReview` types
- `types.RequestState_PENDING`, `types.RequestState_APPROVED`, `types.RequestState_DENIED` states
- Client methods: `NewWatcher()`, `SubmitAccessReview()`, `CreateAccessRequestV2()`

**No types or enums found for:**
- `SessionTracker`, `ModeratedSession`, `ParticipantRequest`, or `SessionEscalation` 
- `KindSessionJoin`, `KindModerationRequest`, or similar watch kinds
- Any session-specific review submission methods

### 4. Session event handling in televibe

**televibe does NOT handle session-related events.** Evidence:
- `/Users/steve.briggs/projects/operations/apps/televibe/app.go:122-124` watches **only** `types.KindAccessRequest`
- No code references sessions, moderation, escalations, or participant requests
- The `handleRequest()` method signature accepts only `types.AccessRequest`, not any session type
- The `submitReview()` method calls only `SubmitAccessReview()` for access requests

**Conclusion:** The Teleport API v0.0.0-20260423131902 in this project does not yet expose session escalations as a first-class resource type like it does for access requests. To handle session escalations in televibe, you would need a newer Teleport API SDK version that adds `KindSessionEscalation` or similar to the watcher, new event types, and corresponding `SubmitSessionReview()` or equivalent client methods.
